title: Keynote Presentation: How the U.S. is Leading the Onshoring and Financing of Minerals and Midstream Projects
gist: The text is a member-only video listing page, not a transcript: a 16-minute Giga Africa 2026 keynote by Widad Whitman of the U.S. DOE's Office of Critical Minerals, Materials, and Manufacturing on how the U.S. is onshoring and financing minerals and midstream projects. No programme details or dollar figures are included.

themes.theme: U.S. onshoring and financing of midstream

insights.claim: The U.S. Department of Energy presents itself as leading the onshoring and financing of minerals and midstream (processing) projects.
insights.speaker: Widad Whitman, Head of Supply Chain Security, Office of Critical Minerals, Materials, and Manufacturing, U.S. DOE
entities: Office of Critical Minerals, Materials, and Manufacturing
insights.so_what: U.S. government financing is a direct catalyst for midstream processing projects; developers aligned with U.S. supply chains gain access to state capital.
insights.quote: How the U.S. is Leading the Onshoring and Financing of Minerals and Midstream Projects

insights.claim: DOE has a dedicated head of supply chain security within its Office of Critical Minerals, Materials, and Manufacturing, showing critical-minerals policy is institutionalised as a security function.
insights.speaker: Widad Whitman, Head of Supply Chain Security, Office of Critical Minerals, Materials, and Manufacturing, U.S. DOE
insights.so_what: Institutionalisation implies durability of U.S. critical-minerals support across political cycles.
insights.quote: Head of Supply Chain Security for the Office of Critical Minerals, Materials, and Manufacturing

insights.claim: A U.S. onshoring keynote being delivered at an Africa conference implies the U.S. approach pairs domestic processing with sourcing from allied African producers.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Minerals
insights.so_what: African miners may be pulled into U.S.-financed supply chains feeding U.S. midstream capacity.
